items.title: Section: Rest From Fatigue, and All Eight Remaining Contexts Close Together

items.zh: 復如有一，於其熱分極炎暑時，或為熱逼、或為劬勞，便生疲倦，非時惛寐，樂著睡眠，是名勞睡。若復於行，廣說乃至於解勞睡所有自相，能正了知。於所應行，乃至於應所解勞睡，能正了知。於應行時，乃至於應解勞睡時，能正了知。如所應行，乃至如所應解勞睡，能正了知。是名正知。彼由成就此正知故，於其自行乃至於其自解勞睡，正知而行乃至正知而解勞睡；若所應行乃至若所應解勞睡，即於彼行乃至於彼解於勞睡；若時應行乃至若時應解勞睡，即此時行乃至此時解於勞睡；如所應行乃至如所應解勞睡，如是而行乃至如是而解勞睡。如是名為於行、於住、於坐、於臥、於其覺寤、於語、於默、於解勞睡正知而住。
items.en: It is also like one who, in the hottest part of the hot season, oppressed by heat or worn out from exertion, grows fatigued and, though it is not the proper time, becomes drowsy and takes to sleep — this is called rest from fatigue. Correctly knowing the specific nature of walking, and so on up through rest from fatigue; correctly knowing what is appropriate in each; correctly knowing the proper time for each; correctly knowing that each should be done exactly so — this is clear awareness. This is called clear awareness in walking, standing, sitting, lying down, wakeful activity, speech, silence, and rest from fatigue.

items.zh: 復次，如是正知而住，云何次第？為顯何事？謂如有一，依止如是村邑、聚落、亭邏而住，作是思惟：我今應往如是村邑、聚落、亭邏巡行乞食。如是乞已，出還本處。又於如是村邑等中，或有居家我不應往。何等居家？謂唱令家、或酤酒家、或婬女家、或國王家、或旃荼羅、羯恥那家；或復有家一向誹謗，不可迴轉。或有居家我所應往。謂剎帝利大族姓家、或婆羅門大族姓家、或諸居士大族姓家、或僚佐家、或饒財家、或長者家、或商主家。又有居家我雖應往，不應太早太晚而往。若施主家有遽務時，亦不應往；若戲樂時、若有營搆嚴飾事時、若為世間弊穢法時、若忿競時，亦不應往。

items.title: Section: A Second, Deeper Pass — Travel Safety and the Moon Simile

items.zh: 又如所往，如是應往。不與暴亂惡象俱行，不與暴亂眾車、惡馬、惡牛、惡狗而共同行，不入鬧叢，不蹈棘刺，不踰垣牆，不越坑塹，不墮山岸，不溺深水，不履糞穢。應隨月喻往施主家，具足慚愧，遠離憍傲，盪滌身心，不求利養，不希恭敬。如自獲得所有利養，心生喜悅，如是於他所得利養，心亦喜悅。不自高舉，不輕蔑他，心懷哀愍。
items.en: Furthermore, one should go exactly as one ought to go: not alongside a rampaging, vicious elephant; not alongside a runaway cart, a vicious horse, a vicious ox, or a vicious dog; not into a chaotic crowd; not treading on thorns; not climbing over a wall; not crossing a ditch or pit; not falling from a cliff; not drowning in deep water; not walking through filth. One should approach a patron's house as the simile of the moon suggests — fully possessed of conscience and shame, free of arrogance, with body and mind cleansed, seeking neither gain nor reverence. Just as one feels joy on receiving some gain oneself, one should feel the same joy when another receives it. One should neither exalt oneself nor belittle others, but hold compassion in the heart.

items.title: Four Points of Self-Restraint When Receiving Support

items.zh: 又應如是自持其心，往施主家。豈有出家往詣他所，要望他施非不惠施，廣說乃至要當速疾而非遲緩。又作是心：我於今假往施主家，所受施物應知其量。又我不應利養因緣，矯詐虛誑、現惑亂相、以利求利。得利養已，無染、無愛，亦不耽嗜、饕餮、迷悶、堅執、湎著而受用之。
items.en: One should also restrain the mind in this way when going to a patron's house: how could one who has gone forth visit another expecting to be given something, as though it were owed rather than freely offered — and so on, expecting it to come quickly rather than slowly? One should further think: I go now, for a time, to the patron's house, and should know the proper measure of what is received. And I should not, for the sake of gain, resort to deceit, false pretence, or the display of confusing appearances, using gain to seek further gain. Having received support, one should use it without attachment, without craving, and without indulgence, gluttony, infatuation, rigid grasping, or heedless abandon.

items.zh: 復於已往或正往時，觀見眾色，於此眾色一分應觀，或有一分所不應觀。於不應觀所有眾色，當攝其眼，善護諸根；於所應觀所有眾色，應善住念而正觀察。

items.title: What Not to Look At: Entertainment and Alluring Forms

items.zh: 何色類色所不應觀？謂諸伎樂戲笑歡娛，或餘遊戲所作歌舞音樂等事；如是復有母邑殊勝，幼少盛年，美妙形色；或復有餘所見眾色，能壞梵行、能障梵行、能令種種諸惡不善尋思現行。如是色類所有眾色，不應觀視。
items.en: What class of forms should not be observed? Musical performance, laughter and revelry, and other entertainments involving song, dance, and music; likewise, women of striking beauty, youthful and in the prime of life, of lovely form; or any other sights capable of undermining pure conduct, obstructing pure conduct, or provoking various unwholesome deliberations. Forms of this class should not be looked upon.

blocks.text: The first pass through the nine contexts ends with rest from fatigue. Then the treatise goes through them again, more deeply. A passage at 0415b20 is untranslated.

"In the hottest season, oppressed by heat or worn out from exertion, one grows fatigued and, though it is not the proper time, lies down briefly." Even rest is done with awareness. The untranslated passage (0415b20) closes the first pass.

The second pass: going about, one avoids danger: "not alongside a rampaging elephant, a runaway cart, a vicious horse, ox, or dog; not into a chaotic crowd; not treading on thorns; not climbing over a wall". One approaches a patron's house "as the simile of the moon suggests": with conscience and shame, free of arrogance, seeking neither gain nor reverence, and glad when another receives as if one had received oneself. Master Cháng Bǎi: one's compassion extends to all beings, fellow practitioners included.

One does not visit expecting to be given something, as if it were owed, or expecting it quickly; one knows the proper measure; one does not use deceit or "confusing appearances" to seek gain with gain (Venerable Miào Jìng: putting on a show of virtue so that others feel they must give); and what one receives, one uses without craving or gluttony.
Entertainment and alluring forms. Master Cháng Bǎi: going out today, "one sees all kinds of advertisements, vendors, and people dressed to attract"; these are the modern equivalents.

quiz.q: How does "rest from fatigue" differ from sleep in the middle watch, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: rest from fatigue is outside the middle-watch sleep
quiz.why: "In the hottest part of the hot season, oppressed by heat or worn out from exertion, one grows fatigued and, though it is not the proper time, becomes drowsy … this is called rest from fatigue." Venerable Miào Jìng: rest from fatigue is outside the middle-watch sleep, not part of it.

quiz.q: What dangers on the road does the treatise list, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 鬧叢?
options: not walking with vicious elephants, horses, or dogs, not entering 鬧叢, not treading on thorns, not climbing walls; 鬧叢 is either overgrown brush or a chaotic crowd
quiz.why: Not alongside a vicious elephant … not into a chaotic crowd, not treading on thorns, not climbing over a wall. Master Cháng Bǎi gives two readings of 鬧叢: a place overgrown with weeds, or a crowded, chaotic place.

quiz.q: Whom does "holding compassion in the heart" concern, and how do the note and the lectures differ?
options: the note limits it to the patron; Cháng Bǎi: all beings, including fellow practitioners; Miào Jìng: sympathy towards everyone
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: compassion here is towards all beings, fellow practitioners included. Venerable Miào Jìng: feel sympathy for everyone — all must live, not just oneself. The translator's note narrows it to the patron.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "displaying confusing appearances"?
options: fooling people by putting on an appearance of virtue so they feel they must give
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 惑亂 means fooling people — putting on an appearance to show oneself virtuous so that others feel they must make offerings.

quiz.q: What modern examples of forms not to be looked at does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: the many advertisements and scantily dressed people seen when going out
quiz.why: "Forms of this class should not be looked upon." Master Cháng Bǎi: going out, one sees all kinds of advertisements and vendors, and some people dressed very revealingly — these are not to be looked at.
